correctness.rationale: For nonzero generator ideal, \(K[x]\) is a PID, so \((f_1,\ldots,f_\ell)=(d)\). Bézout plus rank subadditivity gives the uniform upper bound \(C=\ell\). If \(d\nmid g\), a root multiplicity gap \(a>b\) and the Jordan block \(J_a(\lambda)\) annihilate every generator but not \(g\), contradicting domination. The all-zero-generator case is immediate. The sharpness example has each generator value of rank \(1\) while \(g(X)\) has rank \(\ell\). No finite experiment is used to infer the theorem.
risks: None affecting the stated field and quantifiers; the theorem is not asserted beyond the stated one-variable setting.

value.rationale: The result isolates a mathematically natural boundary created by the new two-variable counterexample: one variable retains the full nonhomogeneous conjecture for every number of generators, and the proof identifies the exact best generator-count coefficient \(\ell\).
